title: 2018 Porsche 911 GT2 RS Weissach: Aerodynamic Masterpiece

scenes.headline: Most Powerful 911 Ever
scenes.narration: 700 horsepower from a twin-turbocharged 3.8-liter flat-six makes this the most powerful road-legal this one has built.

scenes.headline: Limited Edition Legacy
scenes.narration: Launched as a limited edition, Porsche built around just 1,000 units of the 991-based GT2 RS.

scenes.headline: 3.8L Twin-Turbo
scenes.narration: The GT2 RS's 3.8-liter engine relies on prominent dual air intakes and a carbon fiber cover for cooling, enabling a 0-60 time of just 2.7 seconds.

scenes.headline: Aerodynamic Design
scenes.narration: The dual-element rear wing and carbon fiber air intakes enhance aerodynamics, vital for its track focus.

scenes.headline: Rear-Wheel Drive
scenes.narration: Driving the rear wheels through a 7-speed PDK dual-clutch transmission, this setup promises thrilling performance and precise handling on any circuit.

scenes.headline: $695K Sale
scenes.narration: The 2018 GT2 RS Weissach fetched $695,000 at auction, a testament to its exclusive status and extreme performance metrics.

scenes.headline: Horsepower Advantage
scenes.narration: With 700 horsepower, it surpasses the Lamborghini Huracán's 630 hp, reflecting Porsche's edge in engineering excellence.

scenes.headline: Lightweight Cockpit
scenes.narration: Inside, carbon fiber accents and minimalist door straps emphasize weight savings, complementing the GT2 RS’s performance ethos.

scenes.headline: Ultimate Track Weapon?
scenes.narration: With cutting-edge aerodynamics and extreme power, is the 911 GT2 RS the ultimate track weapon you’d consider for your collection?

script: 700 horsepower from a twin-turbocharged 3.8-liter flat-six makes this the most powerful road-legal this one has built. Launched as a limited edition, Porsche built around just 1,000 units of the 991-based GT2 RS. The GT2 RS's 3.8-liter engine relies on prominent dual air intakes and a carbon fiber cover for cooling, enabling a 0-60 time of just 2.7 seconds. The dual-element rear wing and carbon fiber air intakes enhance aerodynamics, vital for its track focus. Driving the rear wheels through a 7-speed PDK dual-clutch transmission, this setup promises thrilling performance and precise handling on any circuit. The 2018 GT2 RS Weissach fetched $695,000 at auction, a testament to its exclusive status and extreme performance metrics. With 700 horsepower, it surpasses the Lamborghini Huracán's 630 hp, reflecting Porsche's edge in engineering excellence. Inside, carbon fiber accents and minimalist door straps emphasize weight savings, complementing the GT2 RS’s performance ethos. With cutting-edge aerodynamics and extreme power, is the 911 GT2 RS the ultimate track weapon you’d consider for your collection?

sections.Highlights: THIS... is a 2018 Porsche 911 GT2 RS Weissach, finished in Guards Red with a black interior. The odometer on this 911 GT2 RS currently displays approximately 3,900 miles. The attached Carfax history report lists no accidents or mileage discrepancies in this Porsche's past. According to the build sheet provided in the gallery, notable factory equipment includes the Weissach Package, 20-inch front and 21-inch rear magnesium wheels, PCCBs, a front axle lift system, an extended range fuel tank, leather and Alcantara upholstery, carbon fiber full bucket seats, and a Bose sound system. Notable modifications reported by the selling dealer are limited to black-finished brake calipers. Launched for 2018 as a limited-edition model, the 991-based GT2 RS stood proud as the most powerful road-going 911 ever released. Porsche went to significant lengths to make the model as light as possible -- it notably fitted lighter springs, numerous carbon fiber parts, and cloth interior door handles. The optional Weissach Package -- which this car is equipped with -- saved an additional 40 pounds. Most sources agree that Porsche built around 1,000 units of the 991-based 911 GT2 RS. Power comes from a twin-turbocharged 3.8-liter flat-6, rated at 700 horsepower and 553 lb-ft of torque. Output is sent to the rear wheels via a 7-speed PDK dual-clutch automatic transmission.
sections.Equipment: A build sheet is provided in the photo gallery, and a partial list of notable equipment reported by the seller includes: Weissach Package Chrono Package with preparation for Lap Trigger 20-inch front and 21-inch rear magnesium wheels in black Porsche Ceramic Composite Brakes (PCCB) Front axle lift system Rear axle steering Extended range fuel tank Leather and Alcantara upholstery Carbon fiber full bucket seats Bose sound system
sections.Seller Notes: The selling dealer notes that the paint protection film has been applied to exterior panels. The selling dealer states that the magnesium wheels were uninstalled early in the vehicle's life and have been reinstalled in preparation for the sale, and that its Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2 tires have about 9/32 of tread.
